transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

Well, doctor, it's just... I can't seem to keep my mind on one thing anymore, and it's really starting to become a problem at work. I work at a distribution warehouse, moving freight and stocking materials, you know? It's a big place, very loud, lots of moving parts. I've been doing it for a while, but lately, every little thing just pulls my attention away. Like, I'll be right in the middle of counting a pallet of boxes, trying to get the inventory numbers right, and then—beep beep beep—a forklift backs up three aisles over. And instead of just ignoring it like I used to, I'm suddenly looking over there, wondering what they're moving, who's driving, if they're going to come down my aisle. Or someone drops a clipboard, or the PA system crackles, or a truck horn goes off outside by the loading dock. It's like my brain just latches onto every single sound or movement. And by the time I look back at my clipboard or my scanner, I've completely lost my place. I'll think I was on box forty-two, but maybe it was fifty-two? And then I realize later, after the shift is over or when a supervisor checks, that I've gone and put the completely wrong numbers into the inventory system. It's embarrassing, really, because I know how to do my job, but it's like my brain is just jumping around like a pinball every time a beeper goes off or someone moves a pallet. I just can't filter it out anymore, and it's making a mess of my work.
Have you noticed yourself feeling more restless or impulsive lately, like you can't sit still or you're acting without thinking?

Restless? Yes. Oh, absolutely. It's actually funny you use that word, because my husband just said the exact same thing to me on Tuesday. Or maybe it was Wednesday? Anyway, usually, after eight or nine hours standing on the concrete floor at the warehouse—and I'm 57, you know, moving freight and hauling boxes isn't exactly a desk job—I come home and I am just dead on my feet. Normally, I just drop my steel-toes by the door, heat up whatever leftovers are in the fridge, and collapse on the couch to watch the evening news. That's been my routine for years. 

But lately... I don't know, it's like I have this motor running inside me that just won't shut off. I come home from a full, exhausting shift and instead of being worn out like usual, I am just buzzing. Just completely wired. I'll walk in the door and instead of sitting down, I'm suddenly pulling everything out of the kitchen cabinets. I spent three hours the other night wiping down the contact paper on the shelves and alphabetizing the spices. Alphabetizing! And then, when I finished that, I went straight out to the garage and started sorting all those plastic storage bins we keep out there. You know the ones? The big heavy totes with the gray lids. I was dragging them around, sorting old holiday decorations and loose screws and gardening tools until past midnight. 

I tried to go inside and just sit on the couch for five minutes, I really did, but it felt completely impossible. My legs were just twitching, and my brain was telling me, 'No, get up, you have to keep moving, you can't just sit here.' It's just this constant, buzzing energy, and I just can't seem to force myself to be still anymore, even when I know I should be exhausted.
Have you noticed that you've needed less sleep lately, or that your mood has been unusually high, excited, or overly confident, even when you're clearly overextending yourself?

Well, I guess the sleep ties into what I was just saying about the garage, but mostly it's just this... this mood I get into. Some days I wake up and I just feel so incredibly upbeat. Honestly, almost too upbeat, if that makes any sense? Like, I'll be driving to the warehouse, drinking my thermos of coffee—just regular drip coffee, I don't do those fancy espresso things—and I will start thinking about how I could completely reorganize the entire loading dock. I get this whole master plan in my head, thinking I can fix the whole workplace, streamline the entire inventory system before my lunch break, and then come home and fix the whole house before dinner! I just feel this rush of confidence, like everything is crystal clear and I can take on the world and get a hundred things done in a single day. 

But the problem is, if anyone gets in my way or slows me down... well, that is a completely different story. Take my husband, for instance. We have been married a long time, and he is a very patient man, but he just doesn't move at my speed lately. The other day I was telling him about my plan to completely redo the landscaping in the front yard, pull up all the old bushes and put in a brick retaining wall, and he just asked me if I really thought we had the time and energy for that right now. And I just... I completely snapped at him. Over something so small! I practically bit his head off, telling him he is always dragging me down and ruining my momentum. Which really isn't fair to him, I know it isn't, but in that moment, I just felt so fiercely irritated that he was questioning my plans when I felt so incredibly capable. I go from feeling like I am absolutely unstoppable, ready to conquer every project under the sun, to just lashing out at him if he so much as breathes a word of doubt. It is like a switch flips and I just can't tolerate anyone questioning me.
Have you had any distinct periods where your mood was so high, irritable, or energized that it was noticeably different from your usual self, even if it didn't last very long?

Well, yes, this whole... whatever you want to call it, this whole phase of being so revved up and snapping at my husband and wanting to rebuild the yard and reorganize the warehouse... it's been going on for about a month now. Exactly a month, I'd say. And it's funny, because I can pinpoint almost the exact day it started, because it lines up right with when my husband stopped working outside the home. He was doing some consulting work, part-time, but he finally decided to just fully retire and be home all day. 

And you know, we've had our routine for so long. For years! We'd both get up, have our coffee, go our separate ways, and then come back together in the evening. But now, he's just... he's there all the time. Our whole daily rhythm just completely changed overnight. I thought it would be nice, having him around more, but instead, it's like this switch flipped inside me right around that same time. Ever since he started staying home about four weeks ago, I've just been on this completely different wavelength. It's like my normal self went out the window the minute our usual schedule disappeared, and I've been stuck in this high-gear, irritable, non-stop mode for the entire month since. It's just so strange how a change in routine like that could set off this whole month-long ordeal, don't you think? Because before he retired, I was just my regular old self, coming home tired and sitting on the couch, and now... well, now it's been thirty days of this buzzing energy and picking fights over retaining walls.

These symptoms align with a hypomanic episode, which is a key feature of bipolar II disorder. Other candidates (e.g., F30.1, F06.8 variants) have been ruled out based on the absence of full manic episodes (ruling out F30.1) and lack of evidence for substance or medical causes (ruling out F06.8 variants).
